common: No coordinator answered on this network.
Check that `mas coordinator start` is running on the other computer and shows a discovery port.
Check that both computers are on the same Wi-Fi or the same cable network and the same subnet; a guest network, a VPN or a different router usually separates them.
Some routers isolate Wi-Fi clients from each other (called client isolation or AP isolation); it is a router setting only you can change.
If you know the coordinator's address, `--coordinator HOST:PORT` skips discovery.
windows: On this Windows computer, the network profile must be Private, not Public: Settings, Network & internet, open the Wi-Fi or Ethernet network, then Network profile type, then Private. The Public profile blocks the replies.
darwin: On a Mac, if the firewall is on, allow incoming connections for Python when macOS asks; System Settings, Network, Firewall.
linux: On Linux, a firewall may drop the replies; allow the discovery UDP port from your own subnet (the exact command depends on your firewall tool).

common: If the coordinator computer's firewall asks whether to allow incoming connections, accept it, or discovery and pairing cannot reach it.
windows: On the coordinator, Windows asks the first time: allow on Private networks only.
darwin: On the coordinator Mac, choose Allow in the incoming connections prompt.
linux: On the coordinator, allow the discovery UDP port and the pairing TCP port from your own subnet.

common: No private network interface is up on this computer, so there is nothing to send on. Connect to your Wi-Fi or cable network, then try again. Virtual interfaces (VPN, containers) are skipped unless you pass --include-virtual.
This computer refused to send the discovery query. A local firewall or security product may be blocking the program from using the network.
windows: Allow Python through Windows Security on Private networks, then try again.
